title: A Mind Duel!
transcript: Chess is like a sword's fight, but instead of swords, we fight with our minds. And whoever's mind is sharper is going to cut deeper. In this position, both players have played an intense game and arrived to this position where they're both left with only two pieces each. And the first one to be able to capture a piece is going to be able to win the game. White starts with king to G4, creating a double attack on both bishops. So, the only way that black can save the bishops is to create a threat of his own with bishop to F1. Now, of course, if white captures, after this capture, this game is going to end in a draw. So, that's not acceptable. So, instead, Sir Lancelot plays rook to H1, maintaining a double attack on the bishops. Now, if black persists with bishop to G2, the rook is actually going to go to G1. You cannot attack it with this bishop because you're just going to lose material. And if you try to go after the knight, knight to C4 is going to make sure that one of the bishops falls. So, instead, black goes to D2 right away, now attacking the white knight. And white, of course, cannot go here because the black bishop is defending. So, instead, it goes to B3, now again attacking both bishops. Now, if black tries to give a check, this is a pretty simple win. After the king moves, there are no more checks in the position, and black has to keep the threats alive. But the rook can come here, and now both bishops are hanging. The bishop comes back, and after rook to F2, it is going to be certain that one of the two is going to fall. So, instead, black just tries to save the dark-square bishop. After all, the bishop is not under attack at the moment. And the bishop has to stay on this diagonal because otherwise, the rook was going to be able to pin the other bishop. But finally, white is able to deliver the final blow with the knight to D3. This creates an unstoppable threat. It's attacking the light-square bishop, and it is threatening to fork the dark-square bishop and the king. The only two squares from which this bishop would be able to stop the fork, are defended by the knight. So, black has no other option but to try and save one of the bishops. And after knight to c6, the dark square bishop is going to fall. And now white has enough material to win this game.
